subject: Eval runway — access orchestration & closing checkpoints
messages:
From: Amira Hassan <amira@helixhealth.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Cc: Infra Team <infra@helixhealth.com>
Date: 2027-11-12T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Eval runway access & network questions

Hi Karthik,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team is excited to run a short evaluation against a subset of our clinical ingestion pipeline. Before we kick off the work we need clarity on a few access pieces so we can create the MAP on our side:

- API key provisioning: do you issue scoped keys per org/env or a single project key for the POC?
- Org setup: any naming conventions you recommend for tenant IDs and environment labels?
- IP allowlist: we can open a CIDR range but need the format you expect. Do you support both IPv4 and customers behind NAT?
- VPC peering: what’s the smallest set of routing rules required for the eval (no cross-account access to other workloads)?

Can you send a short checklist we can slot into our security review? Goal is to start traffic by Nov 22 if possible.

Thanks,
Amira Hassan
Senior Product Manager, Helix Health

From: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Amira Hassan <amira@helixhealth.com>
Cc: grace_oconnor@redwood.ai, tessa_morgan@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-11-13T11:04:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Eval runway access & network questions

Amira — thanks for the clear list. I pulled the engineering and security notes together and put a short orchestration plan below plus the actions we recommend adding to the MAP. Attaching a checkpoint matrix to map responsibilities.

Quick answers up-front:
- API keys: we can issue scoped API keys per "org" and create environment tags (eval-staging, eval-prod) so you can rotate independently. For short-lived evals we typically issue a time-limited key (14 days) and a longer one for sustained POCs.
- Org setup: recommended pattern: <company>-<env>-<team> (e.g., helix-eval-ingest). Using that helps our logs and cost allocation.
- IP allowlist: we accept CIDR blocks in standard v4 notation. For NAT'd environments provide the egress CIDR or a range that covers your NAT gateway. We can also accept single IPs.
- VPC peering: minimal routes required are the peering connection and a rule to allow outbound 443 to the Redwood service subnets. We don't require broad internal routing — just the service subnet and your egress IPs.

Suggested MAP milestones (high level):
1) Week 0 (Nov 12–15): finalize CIDR and owner's contact + sign-off on limited-data terms.
2) Week 1 (Nov 16–22): create org in Redwood, issue time-limited API key, provide allowlist + confirm peering readiness.
3) Week 2 (Nov 23–29): smoke tests, basic throughput run, and quality check.
4) Week 3 (Nov 30): close decision checkpoint (go/no-go) and next-step proposal.

Owners we suggest: Helix infra to provide CIDR & peer config (Liam), Redwood infra (Grace) to share peering guide and open peering request, Redwood dev (Tessa) to issue keys and validate connectivity.

Attachments: eval_runway_checkpoint_matrix.xlsx (milestones/owners) and redwood-vpc-peering-guide.pdf (technical steps).

If this looks good I’ll convert to a MAP doc and put a HubSpot milestone with automated reminders.

— Karthik Iyer
Enterprise Solutions, Redwood Inference

From: Liam Carter <liam.carter@helixhealth.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Cc: Infra Team <infra@helixhealth.com>, Amira Hassan <amira@helixhealth.com>
Date: 2027-11-14T08:22:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Eval runway access & network questions

Karthik — thanks for the clarity. Quick technical notes from infra:

- Preferred egress CIDR: 54.72.16.0/22 (this will be the NAT pool for the eval subnet).
- We will create peering from our VPC vpc-helix-eval to your peering endpoint; our security team will only allow outbound 443 to the Redwood service subnets you provide.
- We need your peering guide and exact service subnet list to set the route. Can you include the minimal firewall rules we should add?

We’ll tag the request helix-eval and target to have peer config ready by Nov 18.

Liam Carter
Cloud Platform Lead, Helix Health
Attachments: (none)

From: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Amira Hassan <amira@helixhealth.com>, Liam Carter <liam.carter@helixhealth.com>
Cc: grace_oconnor@redwood.ai, tessa_morgan@redwood.ai, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-11-15T16:47:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Eval runway access & network questions — next steps & MAP draft

Thanks Liam — that CIDR works. Action items and updated timeline below; I’ll also create the MAP in HubSpot and share the record link.

Action items (owners & due dates):
- Helix: confirm final CIDR and peering contact (Liam) — due Nov 17.
- Redwood: publish exact service subnet list and minimal firewall rules + VPC peering request template (Grace) — due Nov 16.
- Redwood: issue time-limited API key (Tessa) once peering is scheduled — target stage Nov 18.
- Both: perform smoke test and validate TLS handshake & KV cache behavior (joint) — Nov 23–24.

Closing checkpoint: Nov 30 decision meeting (30 minutes) to confirm pass/fail against evaluation criteria in the attached checkpoint matrix. If pass, we’ll provide a short proposal for Dedicated capacity and an estimated cost run-rate for the measured throughput.

Links: HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/6789123 
Drive folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aB2cXYZ-vpc-docs

Attachments included in this thread: eval_runway_checkpoint_matrix.xlsx, redwood-vpc-peering-guide.pdf, temp-api-key-instructions.txt

If you prefer, I can schedule a 30-minute alignment call tomorrow to walk the infra steps with your team.

Thanks — looking forward to getting traffic flowing.

— Karthik Iyer
Enterprise Solutions, Redwood Inference
